interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between React Server Components (RSC) and Client Components?
interviewQuestions.answer: React Server Components execute strictly on the server during build or request time, can directly access databases/filesystems, and add 0kb of JavaScript to the client bundle. Client Components (declared with 'use client') execute on both server (for initial HTML) and browser, enabling browser APIs, event listeners (onClick), and hooks (useState, useEffect).

interviewQuestions.question: How does React's Reconciliation and Virtual DOM algorithm work?
interviewQuestions.answer: When state changes, React constructs a new virtual DOM tree and compares it to the previous tree using a heuristic O(n) diffing algorithm. Elements of different types produce entirely new trees; keys uniquely identify list items across renders to prevent unnecessary re-mounting and preserve DOM state.

interviewQuestions.question: When should you use useCallback versus useMemo?
interviewQuestions.answer: useMemo caches the result of an expensive calculation between renders. useCallback caches a callback function instance between renders, useful when passing callbacks to memoized child components (React.memo) or as dependencies in useEffect to prevent infinite loops.

interviewQuestions.question: What causes the 'Hydration failed' error in SSR applications?
interviewQuestions.answer:
Hydration errors occur when the pre-rendered HTML sent by the server does not match the initial client render tree. Common causes include inspecting window/localStorage during initial render, non-deterministic dates/times (new Date()), invalid nested HTML (e.g.
